sources.title: Historical presidency record: first term, 10 December 2007 to 10 December 2011
sources.findings: Read Casa Rosada’s historical first-presidency record. It dates the first term from 10 December 2007 to 10 December 2011 and identifies her as a lawyer and Frente para la Victoria politician. Its historical office labels are not current appointments. The 2020 page publication or migration date is not an inauguration date. Néstor Kirchner is her presidential predecessor, whereas Alberto Fernández is her later presidential running mate and predecessor as PJ leader.

sources.title: Historical presidency record: birth and second term ending 9 December 2015
sources.findings: Read Casa Rosada’s second-presidency record. It gives birth on 19 February 1953 in La Plata and a second term from 10 December 2011 through 9 December 2015. Preserve the archive’s endpoint rather than silently substituting the following day’s handover. Cabinet members’ dates sometimes run to 10 December and are not her own term endpoint. Her spelling varies between Elizabet and Elisabet in institutional sources; use the established display name and do not invent a distinct identity.

sources.publisher: Universidad Nacional de La Plata, archives
sources.title: Authority record: birth and provincial and national legislative service
sources.findings: Read the UNLP archive authority record, which gives Tolosa and 19 February 1953, provincial legislative service in Santa Cruz from 1989 to 1995, and national legislative service in 1995–2007 and 2017–2019. Tolosa is within the La Plata area, not a contradictory country or province. Its present-tense statement that she is vice president since 10 December 2019 is stale; use later term records and current reporting. This authority record is not itself a graduation transcript.

sources.title: Law-degree fact check citing the university’s October 1979 graduation and December diploma statement
sources.findings: Read Chequeado’s law-degree fact check and its quotation of the rector and law dean’s university statement. It distinguishes graduation in October 1979 from issuance of the abogado degree on 10 December 1979. The qualification is a law degree, not an earned doctorate inferred from the Spanish honorific doctora. The degree assertion is supported through the fact-check article; no claim of personally inspecting the original transcript, diploma or university student file. Allegations that she never graduated are not repeated as established facts.

sources.title: Political biography with update through 1 January 2026: offices, policy and legal chronology
sources.findings: Read CIDOB’s political biography, noting that the main version dates to 18 October 2011 and an appended update runs to 1 January 2026. The update confirms the 10 December 2019 vice-presidential start, 10 December 2023 end and 11 December 2024 takeover of the PJ National Council presidency from Alberto Fernández. Later November 2026 reporting is needed for current party office. The biography describes Peronist/Kirchnerist policy development, but its evaluative language, causal macroeconomic judgments and speculative political motives are not adopted as neutral findings. Party leadership is distinct from national executive office.

sources.title: Original Decree 1602/2009: signed 29 October, published 30 October 2009; AUH eligibility
sources.findings: Read the original Decree 1602/2009 header, signature block and relevant operative eligibility provisions. It was signed on 29 October and published on 30 October 2009. It introduced a non-contributory AUH subsystem for eligible children in households unemployed or working in the informal economy, with conditions and exclusions. Universal in the programme name does not mean an unconditional universal basic income. Historical thresholds and payment amounts are not represented as current 2026 rules. Government objectives are not measured poverty-reduction outcomes.

sources.title: Original Law 26741: 3 May 2012, published 7 May; YPF expropriation provisions
sources.findings: Read the original Law 26741 header and Articles 1–9, especially Articles 7 and 8. The law is dated 3 May 2012 and was published on 7 May. It designates a 51% equity interest in YPF held by Repsol for expropriation; that expropriated block is then divided 51% to the national state and 49% to producing provinces. These two percentages refer to different denominators. Do not call it acquisition of all YPF shares, nationalisation of the entire oil industry, or direct national-government ownership of 51% after the allocation. Repsol YPF Gas is a separate entity with different share-class provisions. No claim that the statute itself proved energy self-sufficiency or resolved later compensation litigation.

sources.publisher: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina
sources.title: Resolution 145/2021: official record of the 2019–2023 vice-presidential term
sources.findings: Read Official Gazette Resolution 145/2021. Its recitals record the vice-presidential constitutional term from 10 December 2019 to 10 December 2023, as proclaimed by the Legislative Assembly. The operative decision concerns her renunciation of salary from April 2021, not resignation from office; no such resignation is inferred. CIDOB’s retrospective update confirms the actual term conclusion. The Chamber of Deputies inauguration page timed out and is not claimed as fully inspected.

sources.title: 6 December 2022: Vialidad verdict, six-year sentence, office disqualification and acquittal on association charge
sources.findings: Read the federal public prosecutor’s report of the Vialidad verdict, specifically the convictions and acquittals section. She received six years for fraudulent administration detrimental to public administration and perpetual disqualification from public office. The court also acquitted her of unlawful association in this case. Prosecutors’ twelve-year request, their broader allegations and the sentence imposed are different. Other defendants’ acquittals, sentences and amounts are not assigned to her. The first verdict was on 6 December 2022; the 9 March 2023 date concerned publication of reasons, not a second conviction.

sources.title: 12 November 2026: separate Vialidad 2 defendants; confirmation that first-case judgment became final on 10 June 2025
sources.findings: Read the prosecutor’s 12 November 2026 Vialidad 2 report, especially its retrospective first-case section. It explicitly confirms the 2022 conviction became final on 10 June 2025 when the Supreme Court rejected defence complaints. The page header’s rolling current date is not its article date. New November 2026 plea-agreement sentences concern six other defendants, including Martín Báez, and are not a new conviction or added prison term for Cristina. Updated aggregate confiscation amounts are not asserted as her personal assets or a fresh personal fine.

sources.title: 10 June 2025: Supreme Court rejects appeal; Kirchner denies wrongdoing and alleges political persecution
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ contemporary 10 June 2025 report on the rejected appeal. Use it for the final six-year judgment and her denial of wrongdoing and claim of political persecution, clearly attributed. Its then-future house-arrest decision is superseded by later court and September 2026 records. Its headline prediction that her political era might end is not an established biographical outcome. A public-office ban does not by itself prove the end of party influence or every party office.

sources.title: 21 September 2026: court maintains home detention after compliance review
sources.findings: Read TN’s 21 September 2026 report that the court maintained house arrest after reviewing compliance. This is sentence execution, not release, acquittal, a pardon or a suspended conviction. Court-reported compliance does not establish facts in other pending cases. The exact residence address, building arrangements, visitors and medical appointment details are unnecessary and omitted from the profile. The review is not treated as a new sentence or an extension of the six-year prison term.

sources.title: 24 October 2026 report of the previous day’s opening hearing in Hotesur–Los Sauces
sources.findings: Read the accessible opening paragraphs of El País dated 24 October 2026. They report her remote participation the previous Friday, 23 October, in the opening hearing of the combined Hotesur–Los Sauces trial. Preserve publication date versus event date, virtual participation versus physical court attendance, and alleged money laundering versus a new conviction. Vialidad’s final judgment does not prove every allegation in this separate case. This is not a claim to have watched the hearing or read the full trial record.

sources.title: 17 November 2026: current PJ presidency and unresolved electoral ambitions
sources.findings: Read Data Diario’s 17 November 2026 article, including the paragraph explicitly stating she continues as PJ president under home detention. Use that narrow current-role statement together with CIDOB’s accession chronology. This pre-event article’s planned meetings and invited participants are not evidence of completed attendance. Discussion of a possible 2027 candidacy and a possible future UN response is not a confirmed candidacy, restored eligibility or overturned judgment. Provincial PJ leadership and national party office are distinct.

sources.title: 17 November 2026: visible headline and standfirst report balcony greeting to supporters
sources.findings: Read the visible headline, standfirst and timestamp of Página/12’s 17 November 2026 item, stating that she emerged onto her balcony to greet supporters. The accessible content is a short report accompanying video, not a fully inspected audiovisual record. State this evidence scope in all eight language versions. This actual-appearance report supports recent activity but does not demonstrate release from house arrest, a medical conclusion or a legal change. No crowd-size estimate is independently verified.

portraitReview.unresolved: Read candidate and parent Commons metadata, derivative credit, dual-licensing text, public VRT confirmation and upload history. Candidate is 647×860 and was uploaded/cropped by Maximus0970 on 14 March 2011; parent is 2100×1408. Both metadata pages list 10 December 2010, while old upload descriptions refer to a year-end 2011 message and current caption refers to 2010; exact capture occasion/date requires checking the archived presidential source. Upload date is not capture date. The candidate expressly permits a choice between CC BY-SA 2.0 and CC BY 2.0; use the former and preserve its sharing conditions, institutional attribution and crop notice. Raw metadata’s single CC BY 2.0 value is incomplete rather than inherently false. The December 2015 change in presidential-site licensing does not retroactively relicense older photographs. Private VRT correspondence was not accessed. Original download on 18 November failed with curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; old cache is absent. Portrait identity, colour and crop suitability remain visually unverified.
